newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Merck sees strong 1997 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Merck sees strong 1997 profit growth.

text.p: German drugs group Merck KGaA said on Tuesday its 1996 profits surged 36 percent and said it expected further earnings growth, possibly in double digit percentage points, this year as well.
Describing 1996 as "an extremely successful year," Merck posted net profit of 502 million marks ($297.6 million) for 1996 amid a 10.9 percent rise in sales to 6.95 billion marks.
The news pushed its shares up 2.50 marks, or 3.8 percent, to 68.30 by the end of bourse trade, outperforming the broader market where average gains were below one percent.
Merck management board chairman Hans Joachim Langmann later told a news conference that if sales registered double-digit growth in 1997, then profits would also grow in double-digits.
Langmann gave no dividend outlook for 1997, but said that Merck followed a "shareholder-friendly" route.
Merck's core pharmaceutical business fuelled the 1996 advance, with sales rising 16 percent to 3.9 billion marks to account for 56 percent of group business.
Laboratory sales rose 6.3 percent to 1.7 billion marks while speciality chemicals sales advanced 5.1 percent to 1.3 billion marks.
The company also said it had spent 1.2 billion marks on acquisitions.
The company is to pay a 1.25 mark dividend for 1996. In 1995, Merck paid a dividend of 32 pfennigs for share for the final quarter only.
